template_definition.purpose: Give authors one form for a guide that explains or walks a reader through a stable operating procedure.
template_definition.responsibility: A guide owns how a reader reaches and checks one operating outcome; execution and recovery steps stay with runbooks and rules stay with policies.
non_goals: Executable recovery or release procedures, which belong to a runbook.
Normative rules and approvals, which belong to a policy or governance document.
Granting authority to run any command.
template_definition.applicability: Every operation/guide document under docs/05.operations/guides/ and its template.

positive: GDE-0010 passes the form tree, table, body-contract, author-prompt and residue checks.
A guide whose Steps table keeps the registered columns passes the document table check.
negative: A reordered, missing or extra Steps column fails BODY-TABLE-COLUMNS.
A Lifecycle Traceability table whose keys differ from the body contract fails REGISTRY_TABLE_BODY_CONTRACT.
A table section outside the form fails REGISTRY_TABLE_SECTION.
regression: The loaded guide profiles keep heading lists equal to the form H2 titles.
tests/test_common_form_tree.py asserts exactly the forms and definitions the repository registry carries.

migration.meaning_map: The SPEC-0169 meaning map moves each GDE-0010 sentence into its Purpose, Prerequisites, Procedure or Verification section without changing meaning; the Task records it.
migration.retained_history: Git history retains the previous six-section guide layout and its template.

columns.meaning: Order of the step in the procedure.
What the reader does at this step.
How the reader observes that the step worked.
Link to the Spec or Task that owns the guide lineage, or an N/A reason.
The outcome the guide gives its readers.
The system, workflow or concept the guide covers.

template_definition.purpose: Give authors one form for an incident record that states the confirmed event, its impact, its timeline, its resolution and its evidence.
template_definition.responsibility: An incident record owns the observed facts, timeline, mitigation, recovery verification and evidence of one event; causal analysis and corrective actions belong to the postmortem.
non_goals: Root-cause analysis and corrective-action design, which belong to the postmortem.
Recording a guess as an observed fact or rewriting a historical log.
Granting authority for any live action; a record of an action never authorizes repeating it.
template_definition.applicability: Every operation/incident document under docs/05.operations/incidents/ and its template.

positive: The incident template passes the form tree, table, body-contract, author-prompt and residue checks.
An incident whose Events table keeps the registered columns, or whose Events table has a header only, passes the document table check.
negative: A reordered, missing or extra Events column fails BODY-TABLE-COLUMNS.
A Lifecycle Traceability H3 outside Evidence fails BODY-H3-PARENT.
A Lifecycle Traceability table whose keys differ from the body contract fails REGISTRY_TABLE_BODY_CONTRACT.
A resolved incident whose Recovery Verification holds no concrete evidence fails INCIDENT-RESOLUTION-EVIDENCE.
regression: The loaded incident profiles keep heading lists equal to the form H2 titles.
tests/test_common_form_tree.py asserts exactly the forms and definitions the repository registry carries.
tests/test_native_skill_envelope.py shows INCIDENT-RESOLUTION-EVIDENCE failing without Recovery Verification evidence and passing with it.

migration.meaning_map: The SPEC-0171 incident template map moves each of the ten former H2 sections into the Summary, Impact, Timeline, Resolution or Evidence section without changing meaning; the Task records it.
migration.retained_history: Git history retains the previous ten-section incident template; no incident document exists.

columns.meaning: The zoned time of the observation, decision or action.
What was observed, decided or done at that time.
Who or what observed, decided or acted.
The timeline entry or response action the row covers.
The named incident evidence for it.
The follow-up Task that owns it, or an N/A reason.

template_definition.purpose: Give authors one form for a postmortem that records the root cause, the confirmed impact, the corrective actions and their evidence for one incident.
template_definition.responsibility: A postmortem owns the causal analysis, contributing factors, corrective actions and review decision for one incident; the observed facts and timeline stay in the incident record.
non_goals: Restating the incident timeline, which belongs to the incident record.
Assigning blame to a person; contributing factors are recorded without blame.
Granting authority for any live action; a corrective action never authorizes its own execution.
template_definition.applicability: Every operation/postmortem document under docs/05.operations/incidents/ and its template.

positive: The postmortem template passes the form tree, table, body-contract, author-prompt and residue checks.
A postmortem whose Actions table keeps the registered columns, or whose Actions table has a header only, passes the document table check.
A postmortem with no What Went Well H3 passes, and one with the H3 under Impact and a body passes.
negative: A reordered, missing or extra Actions column fails BODY-TABLE-COLUMNS.
A Lifecycle Traceability H3 outside Corrective Actions or a What Went Well H3 outside Impact fails BODY-H3-PARENT.
A What Went Well H3 with no body fails BODY-SECTION-EMPTY.
A Lifecycle Traceability table whose keys differ from the body contract fails REGISTRY_TABLE_BODY_CONTRACT.
regression: The loaded postmortem profiles keep heading lists equal to the form H2 titles.
tests/test_common_form_tree.py asserts exactly the forms and definitions the repository registry carries.

migration.meaning_map: The SPEC-0171 postmortem template map moves each of the twelve former H2 sections into the Summary, Root Cause, Impact, Corrective Actions or Evidence section without changing meaning; the Task records it.
migration.retained_history: Git history retains the previous twelve-section postmortem template; no postmortem document exists.

columns.meaning: The corrective action that prevents recurrence.
The person or team that owns the action.
How the completion and effect of the action are verified.
The root cause or prevention action the row covers.
The owner and the due date or state of the action.
The follow-up Task that owns it, or an N/A reason.
The requirement, decision, Spec, guide or policy owner that receives the lesson.

template_definition.purpose: Give authors one form for a runbook that carries an operator through one executable operating procedure, its checks and its recovery.
template_definition.responsibility: A runbook owns the preconditions, steps, stop conditions, validation and recovery of one operating procedure; stable explanations stay with guides and rules with policies.
non_goals: Stable explanatory material, which belongs to a guide.
Normative rules and approvals, which belong to a policy or governance document.
Granting authority to run any command; a command or its boundary marker never authorizes execution.
template_definition.applicability: Every operation/runbook document under docs/05.operations/runbooks/ and its template.

positive: Each runbook and the template pass the form tree, table, body-contract, author-prompt, residue and command-boundary checks.
A runbook whose Triggers table keeps the registered columns, or whose Triggers table has a header only, passes the document table check.
negative: A reordered, missing or extra Triggers column fails BODY-TABLE-COLUMNS.
A Recovery Procedures H3 outside Recovery fails BODY-H3-PARENT and an empty one fails BODY-SECTION-EMPTY.
A Lifecycle Traceability table whose keys differ from the body contract fails REGISTRY_TABLE_BODY_CONTRACT.
A table section outside the form fails REGISTRY_TABLE_SECTION.
regression: The loaded runbook profiles keep heading lists equal to the form H2 titles.
tests/test_common_form_tree.py asserts exactly the forms and definitions the repository registry carries.

migration.meaning_map: The SPEC-0170 meaning map moves each runbook sentence into its Purpose, Preconditions, Steps, Validation or Recovery section without changing meaning; the Task records it.
migration.retained_history: Git history retains the previous six-section runbook layout, its four-column step table and its template.

columns.meaning: The condition that makes the operator run the action.
What the operator does when the trigger holds.
How the action is undone, or why it cannot be.
Link to the Spec or Task that owns the runbook lineage, or an N/A reason.
The trigger or control the runbook answers.
Where the evidence is kept or who owns recovery.
